concept: Track Diagram's signal-box line was praised wherever it drew the family's own order, and it lost points on the pages it left as boxes. Branch Lines keeps Home's fortnight line, the lit NOW lamp and the To do timetable, and gives every boxed page a branch of the same diagram drawn from its own data: Chat on a double-track main line, Status's lamps banked on one indication shelf, Ideas as a railway out of home on a log scale, the month as week tracks, and the Plans list, the phone's month and the odd calls on Status as one timetable row. It should feel like an exact, calm signal box at night: steel lines on slate, lamps that say how things stand, and the tube's own light only on what is live.
companions: Steel-cyan #a7c4d8 is the only companion with a job on every page: it is the family's hand and the wiring. It draws the rails (#58697a, dimmed to #2e343b for days gone by), the rings, the family's initial rings and the 3px bar on their bubbles, and the underlined links. Anything selected or latched is a backlit steel key (radial #879dae to #748a9b, dark ink): 'here' in the bar and in the settings nav, the latched Show key, the current tab, an open Edit, today's date on the month. Green-black slate carries every page: #0f1519 boards, #161c20 plates and #080c0d for the indication well. Section and kind colours live only in rings and lamps: cyan is a plan (Coming up, the month's rail lamps and plates, the Plans timetable); lemon is a deadline still to come; amber is late or worth a look (filled lamps, 'was due' words, the late link in a head, the setup edge, the odd calls on Status, 'Needs a look' on Settings) and nothing else, since the restaurants box lost its amber edge and eyebrow; a half amber lamp is partly working; a hollow pewter ring is off; red is kept for Needs attention; each idea's kind colour is its ring. #6dff9c is lit only for now and live: the mark, 'next', Send, the box, the now lamps and the runs from them, working lamps, her screens and the tubes.
decisions: The title stays 'What's *next* for us?', the lineage's best so far: the question a family asks when deciding the weekend, the next outing or the next thing to get done, in their own 'us', one line on a phone, and 'next' is the diagram's own meaning of the lit green (now, and what comes next down the line). It is still the box's <label for="text">, lit with E1's layered halo.

Chat is a double-track main line (L033 rebuilt in steel), now truly two rails: 2px each, 22px apart, leaving her glyph screen in the steel terminus ring at the head. Each message is a station: her 28px screen (now opaque, so the rail no longer shows through it) on the left rail with her words to its left in green-black glass, the family's steel ring and initial on the right rail with their words to its right on a square #1c252b plate with a 3px steel bar. The time is printed across both rails on a #0b0e0c patch; the day is a tie ('Sun 27 Sep'). The rails turn through 45 degrees, meet, and one short lit run ends in the lit ring seated on the composer's top edge, whose own edge now carries a 30% brand breath as Home's box does. The kids' conversations are the family's steel rings with an initial and an underlined name. On the phone it folds to one rail.

Status opens on the indication shelf (L143), banked and linked, beside the spend tube: the tube spans the panel's height, the recessed #080c0d well stretches to the right edge and the full height above the tally, and the tally ('6 working · 7 off', 40px Archivo 600 at width 75) sits on the line of the tube's chin as the shelf's legend, each figure followed by the lamp it counts. Working lamps hold steady (the page's breathing lamp is now's alone). Under the chin only 'Change the limit' (and, when it is reached, the warning); the sentence repeating the tube is gone. Waiting's chips became the tally's figures ('10 looked up · 2 waiting to be looked up'); Worth a look became a timetable of one-line rows, time in the 8.5rem margin, an amber lamp on the rail, as Recent activity now shares that margin. On the phone the banks stack name over lamps inside the gutter, and model names never break.

Ideas draws the line from home (L063 as a railway) in a tube the width of the column: one row of VT323 words across the top that wraps where it must ('The line from home · 10 places · Nearest #7 … 18 min NW · Furthest #4 … 2 h 45 min W'), and under it the railway the whole width of the glass. Home is lit at the left; a break in the rail says the first ten minutes are not to scale; from 10 min the line runs on a log scale (worked out in the template as a ratio of tiny powers, since Jinja has no log) with mileposts at 10, 15, 20, 30 min, 1 h, 2 h and 3 h, so the five places 18-21 minutes out stand about 20px apart and 18-27 minutes spread over some 140px. Numbers alternate above and below and take a short spur where two would touch. The drawing is set in presentation attributes; the sheet only lights it. On the phone only the nearest's, the furthest's and the pointed-at station's numbers show, the words wrap whole, and each row is two lines (title whole; kind and drive).

The month is week tracks (L145): each week's 2px rail is now the line between it and the next (the cells draw no rule of their own, so a week reads as one line, not two), drawn by the page as SVG with each plan's cyan ring at its hour, today's NOW lamp breathing at this hour, and the run from it lit to the next plan with a hot core, fading into the steel through a mask. Past days dim their rail and hollow their lamps; weekend columns sit a step lighter; today's date is a backlit steel key. On the phone the month is a timetable on the same board: the day in the margin, a cyan ring per day to come, today's lit lamp and the run from it, days gone by dimmed with pewter rings.

The Plans list, the page 'All plans' opens, is a timetable too: the NOW lamp breathing at the head of the line with a lit run to the first plan, as on Home's fortnight; each plan one line (day and hour in the margin, a cyan ring, the plan, how far off, where, and Move it / Cancel it as keys); what has been below on a dimmed rail with pewter #56616b rings. 'Put something on the calendar' stands on the title's baseline beside List and Month and opens its form as the link's target (scripts off too).

One timetable row for everything in time that is not the To do list (the Plans list, the phone's month, Status's odd calls): stamp in an 8.5rem margin (5.6rem on a phone, the time under the day), lamp on the rail, one line along it, a steel wash with a sage edge when pointed at. Late is the one amber job.

Every page that lists things puts its figure after the title, a numeral stacked with its unit as the fortnight's day numerals stand beside month and weekday: 'Ideas 12 ideas / 10 on the line', 'Things to do 4 open / 2 late' with '2 late' linking to the first late row, 'Plans 5 coming up / in the next 90 days', and the month's count. The column counts that used to sit in the list heads moved up there.

One label step: whatever names a column, a table, a sub-list or a margin is 13px in sentence case, untracked, in the label's steel (Who, Due, Idea, For, Drive, No., Mon…Sun, By kind of call, By model, Calls that ended oddly); dates and stamps are DM Mono at the same 13px (Wednesday 30 September, Oct / Sun, 3 days ago, 19:47). Capitals are the glass's alone.

Amber has one job again. The restaurants box on Home is one more Lately added row (the restaurant kind's ring, '2 restaurants to try', the arrow), no edge, no eyebrow. Settings rows each carry the Status page's lamp for their part (lit working, half amber partly for Messages, pewter off for Lookups and Connections, none for the change log), and the part that needs a look an amber lamp and the amber words 'Needs a look' instead of a bronze chip and edge.

One drawing for every control: graphite keys for secondary actions, the backlit steel key for anything selected or latched (now the settings nav's 'here' too), green only on the page's one primary; 0 targets under 44px on every rendered page. On a phone To do's rows are two lines (title; who and when) with the Edit key as its icon.

The light, from Aglow, stays on the live list: tubes at 1.0 with bloom and scanlines in a thin 3px graphite case with a hairline lip, vent chin and power lamp; 'next' in E1's halo; Send's ring and pool; Home's box lit at rest; her screens; lamps as white-hot cores in two halos; lit runs whose bloom falls off with them; the row afterglow as a 12% steel wash with a 2px sage edge, in 0.12s and out over 1.2s. The cobalt wash stays off (washGlow 0).

The css is 57.2K of 60K, built from readable sources (src/track.css, phosphor.css, relight.css, branch.css) by src/build.py, which strips comments, drops declarations a later rule for the same selector overrides, writes the palette's fixed colours out (now also mixing colour-mixes of fixed colours and writing rgb() as hex), and shortens the sheet's own property names. Moving the Ideas line and the month's rails into the page's SVG attributes paid for this revision's new rows.
strengths: Six pages now change their drawing, not their paint: Chat, Status, Ideas, the month, the Plans list and Settings each draw their own data in the same steel-on-slate line (who spoke and when, what is working, how far each place is, how long until the next plan, what is coming, how each part stands), which answers the owner's 'reflect more of the page content'.

One line language and one row drawing hold on every page: rails on slate, rings and lamps with one meaning each, a lit run from every now lamp to its next stop (the fortnight, To do, setup, the month, the Plans list, Who answers, the line from home), and one timetable row wherever there is time.
The two rails of Chat read as two now, and the lit ring sits on the box: side, mark and time each say who spoke.

Light carries data and never fills an empty glass: the Ideas tube draws the family's places on a scale that separates the ones twenty minutes out, and the shelf holds every lamp on Status as links to their rows.

Typesetting: one 13px label step in sentence case, mono stamps at the same size, head figures stacked like the day numerals, drives set on the digit with the compass in its own sub-column, tabular figures throughout; caps only on the glass.
0 targets under 44px on every rendered page, desktop and phone; the phone versions of Ideas, the month, the Plans list, Status and To do were checked too.
weaknesses: Still a line-heavy design, now more so: a judge who reads lines as a subway map will find one on nearly every page.
Chat and Status are almost all green and neutral by the measure (97.5% and 99.3% of the coloured pixels green): their grounded colour is steel and slate, which the measure counts as grey.
When Google Calendar is not connected (as in the demo) 'Put something on the calendar' is a graphite key, not the green primary, because the form it opens can only say that nothing can be added here.

Ideas' words differ from today's by 28.3%: prose facts became a drive column, the tube's words changed, and the list's count moved into the head. The drive, the log scale's inputs, the late flag, the month's hours, the settings rows' states and Chat's weekday are all worked out in the templates from the row's words or the app's clock; each is a small field in views.py when it ships.
The row-to-station light on Ideas is one :has() rule per row position, written for the first 16 rows.
The Ideas line's lit run from home to the nearest place still crosses about a quarter of the glass with no station on it, because the nearest place is 18 minutes out.
On the phone the line's stations (18-21 minutes) still sit within a few pixels of each other; only the nearest, the furthest and the pointed-at one are numbered there.
